kevin: We've got a customer repro — rerank API returning 400. They say their app wraps requests in an envelope and it fails intermittently. Paste of their request (redacted):

kevin: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"payload": {"batch": [{"requests": [{"id": "q1", "query": "find best match", "candidates": {"0": {"text": "A"}, "1": {"text": "B"}}}] }]}}'
```

maria: Ah — candidates is an object keyed by index, not an array. That will pass some json parsers but our schema requires an array. 400 likely from our validation layer.

alex: Do we have the exact 400 body?

support-bot: ERROR 400 — Invalid request: "candidates" must be an array of candidate objects. Received object at payload.batch[0].requests[0].candidates

kevin: Customer says they built a small wrapper to support an older SDK and it transforms arrays into maps for deduping. They didn't realize it hit the rerank endpoint.

maria: Quick repro in node: if you do Object.fromEntries(items.map((i, idx) => [String(idx), i])) you get that shape. They probably used that to enforce stable indices.

alex: Can we return a more helpful error? Right now it's "must be an array" but the client only sees 400 and just retries. Might be worth adding a hint like "got object, expected array" with path.

kevin: For the customer, suggested workaround: ensure candidates is an array before sending. Example payload to send:```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "query": "find best match",
      "candidates": [ {"text": "A"}, {"text": "B"} ]
    }
  ]
}
```

maria: Also noted they used nested envelope: payload.batch[0].requests vs the expected top-level items. We accept "items" at top-level or a single batch, but deep nesting may bypass some middleware. I left a note to docs to call out allowed shapes.

ops-bot: @kevin I queued a quick validation rule to log object->array coercions for 24h to capture if other clients do this.

kevin: Customer confirmed fix works after sending candidates as an array. Marking as resolved, will follow up to tighten error message. :white_check_mark:
